title: hazel-jit’s PR, Described
blurb: A working draft of the description for hazelgrove/hazel#2859, hazel-jit for dev, to iterate on before it goes on GitHub: an executive summary for whoever decides, an engineering summary for whoever reviews, then the details. Every evaluator test also runs compiled where it compiles: 234 of 289 do, and none differs from the interpreter. Beside ReScript, Melange and js_of_ocaml, hazel-jit now lays out records as they do, as plain objects. Four ways on the games of hazeljs-examples: hazel-jit now runs their rules 4,148 times as fast as the interpreter and 3.1 times as fast as on 2026-11-19, and takes 3.8 times the time of the same game written by hand in JavaScript, where it took 11.9 times. Gnome world's speed run, timed three ways: 44,933 steps in 25.5 s with hazel-jit now, 24.7 s in plain JS, about 4.2 minutes interpreted; the rules are 1.3% of it with hazel-jit, the water most of the rest. With the day's changes merged: tail calls as loops, a named function's tuple parts as JS arguments, constructors without arguments made once, a module's members by name; and where conversion at the edges still costs, and how to bring it down.
